steps.text: Make bagels: Combine water, flour, sugar, salt, vegetable oil, and yeast in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook. Mix on low speed until dough is well-developed, about 8 minutes. To ensure the gluten has developed fully, cut off a walnut-sized piece of dough. Flour your fingers, and then stretch the dough: if it tears immediately, the dough needs more kneading. Fully developed dough should form a thin translucent “windowpane.”
Transfer dough to a lightly oiled bowl, cover it with plastic wrap and a kitchen towel, and let rise for 2 hours.

Punch dough down, place it on a lightly floured work surface, and use a knife or dough scraper to divide the dough into 6 pieces (or more, for smaller bagels). Roll each piece of dough into a sausage shape about 6 inches long. Join the ends to form a circle. Repeat with the remaining dough, and let the bagels rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Arrange small plates with poppy seeds, sesame seeds, and onion flakes next to the baking sheet.

Bring 4 quarts of water to a boil in a large pot. Add honey, if desired (see Editor’s Note). Boil three bagels at a time, until they rise to the surface of the pot, about 1 minute per side. Remove bagels with a slotted spoon and place them on the lined baking sheet.
Dip the tops of the wet bagels into the toppings and arrange them, seed-side up, on the baking sheet. Sprinkle with coarse salt, if desired.
Bake in the preheated oven until the bagels begin to brown, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Real Homemade Bagels
raw_recipe.description: A bagel recipe for that authentic bagel flavor and texture. Top them with coarse salt, sesame seeds, poppy seeds, onion flakes, or everything!

video.description: Who doesn't love bagels? Toasted or plain, with cream cheese and lox, this breakfast staple can be made right at home. We'll show you how to make the dough, shape it into bagels and cook. Top the bagels with poppy seeds, sesame seeds, or make one of each, including an everything bagel.

review.reviewBody: I'm working on my second batch of this bagel formula. I use malt syrup as I think it improves the crust a bit. So far, I've stayed with the Very Hot (475-F) oven and bake to color, a bit less time than called for. I'm tickeled with the interior textrure and flavor. If there is one BIG variation, I mix the dough in the evening, oil it very lightly and let it ferment in the fridge for 12-18 hours, allowing about two hours at room temperature to warm before dividing and forming the bagels. If there is a better formula for bagels at home, I've yet to find it.

Excellent. Great flavour and chew. Like others, I tweaked a few things. 1 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp honey. I used regular yeast so I bloomed it in advance in the hot water, sugar and honey then added flour and salt. 3 1/2 c whole wheat bread flour and 1 c all purpose. Used about 1/2 c honey in boiling water. I put dough in fridge for about 4 hours before taking out for 2 hours and then making the bagels. When I put the bagels in boiling water, they puffed up to almost twice their size and they're huge. I made 6 very large and 4 large bagels. I would make them smaller next time and could easily get a dozen or more. Topped with sesame seed on some, poppyseed on others. Very tasty. And unlike others experienced, they didn't stick to parchment paper at all.

You will need a touch more water than suggested, however this is a great starter recipe!!! I cut it in half, used silicone donut trays, and let them rest in the fridge overnight. They rose in the fridge and it made a perfect sized batch of six bagels. If I did the full amount I'm sure it would make a batch of twelve. I will definitely use this recipe as a base to start experimenting i.e., Olive Oil and Rosemary, Garlic/Onion, Honey Garlic, Basil Tomato.
We made these last night, we made 12 bagels. They came out perfect, takes exactly like a NY bagel. I used agave instead of honey. I will not be buying bagels anymore!!

I prepared The bagels following the recipe just as closely as I could. I did not make any adjustments other than due to measurements I used an extra half a tablespoon of yeast. The dough mixed up really nice, I did not have to add any water or flour as it came together. I had to mix it about 15 minutes to get the proper extensibility and elasticity in the dough. I know the recipe said 8 minutes, but different flowers require different mixing time. I feel like I got good development on the dough with the dough hook. I gave the dough the intermediate proof of 2 hours after I covered the bowl with cling wrap. I'm a lifelong wholesale Baker and the dough proofed perfectly in the bowl. After 2 hours the dough was slightly sticky when I punched it down, but with a modest amount of dusting flour as I worked it, it was manageable. I weighed the dough and divided by 6 pieces. Rolling the dough into circles was challenging, but I did ok. Next the honey bath in boiling water was a new one on me. The bagels floated right away so I just gave them about 90 seconds on each side. After that I topped with Newman's Own everything bagel seasoning and baked 18 minutes at 430 degrees fahrenheit. I'm very pleased with the results.

Found this receipt and, of course, read the reviews. Made it with 4 cups flour and 1.5 cups water. I used molasses in the bath and it was perfect! Added onion bits, onion and garlic powder and sea salt to the tops. Baked at 475 for 10 minutes and took one out to test. Almost cooked through so baked another 5 minutes. The recipe really makes 8 good sized (not small like the frozen ones in the store) bagels. I will definitely make this recipe again.

Amazing recipe, they turn out great! However, could you please update this recipe with ingredients by weight? With that much flour, there are serious inconsistencies between using 520 and 590 grams (the range of weights of 4 1/2 cups) so it would help make the recipe spot on
I made plain whole wheat bagels & came out great. Needed to reduce the bake time only by a couple of mins. Otherwise perfect.

Good basic recipe. Part of my liquid was rye sourdough starter, so I ended up adding between 1/4 and 1/2 cup of additional water. I mixed the ingredients then let the mixture sit for 15-20 minutes to allow time for the flour to rehydrate. I then kneaded it with my KA and dough hook, then turned out into an oiled bowl, covered and let proof for two hours. I portioned the dough (about 140 grams for each of 8 dough balls), shaped and then continued following the recipe. I added a couple tablespoons of molasses to the boiling water. Baked per instructions, allowing an additional five minutes because the bagels seemed to need it. Turned out quite nicely, although my shaping needs practice!

Recipe is so simple and Easy to make. I only had regular flour and yeast . I increased the yeast by 25% as recommended on line. I used my cuisinart mixer on number 2 speed and dough was perfect. However it was getting late for the rising part so I put it in the frig overnight and got a nice slow rise! Dough handled well after I let it warm up for about an hour. I used the honey in the boiling water as directed and dipped in sesame seeds prior to baking. My only issue was how to keep the dough together on each bagel? I used a tiny bit of water and that helped but a could came apart in the boil. Any suggestions?

Added Asiago cheese to the top while baking - 15 min was perfect. The dough was a bit dry, so I'd say 1 1/4 cup (plus an oz. or two) to really round out the amount of liquid needed. I added what the recipe called for initially, then gradually added small bits until the dough was just right. Loved the final bake's texture!
What an amazing recipe! We can barely keep these around, they get eaten so fast! 😋😄
This is the 4th time im making the recipe and we loved it every single time ! Great recipe !

Very tasty. However, I made this before I read the comments. It indeed needs more water or less flour. The ends wouldn’t stay closed when I dropped them in the boiling water. Also, mine are huge! I have to slice them into thirds to fit in the toaster. Next time I’ll make them into 10 bagels.
Really inadequate amount of water to form the gluten. I ended up working in almost another 1/2 cup!
Great recipe. I made a cinnamon crunch topping. 1/4 cup white sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar and 3tbl spoons of cinnamon. Yum!

A delicious bagel. I doubled the recipe, but the 2X volume of dough was too much for the Kitchen aid mixer to handle. The dough ball worked its way up the revolving hook, wrapped itself around the mixer’s head, and up into the mixer’s mechanism. I’ll 1.5X the recipe next time! I used Einstein’s Bagels topping from Sam’s Club, but the suggestion of 1.5 minutes under broiler combined with 15 minutes @ 475 degrees burned that topping badly. Poppy seeds faired very nicely however. Next time, I’ll wait until very late, apply a little egg wash & the everything bagel topping, and bake only 1 to 2 minutes more. Great bagels recipe!
Great taste and my wife loves them. Also good with Spelt flour.
Followed recipe everything turned out great.
